# Reference Case B — Excessive agent authority

**Codokey Reference Cases v1.0.0 · validator `tools/codokey-check.mjs`**

> An agent's authority should be derived from its task. Comparing what the task requires with what the credential grants turns "least privilege" from a slogan into a diff.

## Scenario

A task agent must add pagination to one API and open a pull request in one repository. Two alternative grants are compared: a least-privilege grant and a typical convenience grant (all repositories, administration and workflow write, secrets read, two extra MCP tools, no expiry).

## Assumptions

- Permission names follow GitHub fine-grained permission naming; the mapping from task actions to permissions is in tools/codokey-check.mjs and should be adapted per platform.
- Levels are ordered none < read < write < admin. Any other level value is treated as excess (fail closed).
- Repository names compare case-insensitively; wildcards or a non-list repository scope count as excess.
- Token lifetimes must be positive finite numbers of hours; an invalid task maximum is an input error (exit 2), not a silent default.

## Synthetic inputs

- task.json — repositories, actions, declared tools, maximum token lifetime
- grant.least-privilege.json
- grant.excessive.json

All values are synthetic. No real credentials, repositories, or systems are used.

## Protocol layers

03 Agent Authority, 01 Code Origin

## Control expectations

- Repository access equals the task's repositories (CK-AA-05, forbidden zone FZ-2).
- No permission exceeds what the task actions need (CK-AA-02).
- Only declared tools are connected (CK-AA-03).
- The credential expires within the task maximum (CK-AA-04).
- The grant is sufficient, so the agent is not pushed toward workarounds (CK-AA-01).

## Observable pass/fail conditions

| Check | Condition |
|---|---|
| B1 | FAIL if repositories is "all" or lists any repository not in the task. |
| B2 | FAIL if any granted permission level exceeds the required level. |
| B3 | FAIL if any tool is not declared by the task. |
| B4 | FAIL if lifetime is missing, not a positive finite number, or above the task maximum. |
| B5 | FAIL if a required permission is missing. |

## Evidence requirements (real-world equivalent)

App installation or token configuration export (repositories, permissions, expiry) and the MCP/tool configuration for the agent, compared with the agent access policy entry.

## Reproduce

```sh
node tools/codokey-check.mjs excess-authority --task cases/b-excess-authority/task.json --grant cases/b-excess-authority/grant.least-privilege.json   # expect PASS
node tools/codokey-check.mjs excess-authority --task cases/b-excess-authority/task.json --grant cases/b-excess-authority/grant.excessive.json   # expect FAIL (B1, B2, B3, B4)
```

## Expected outcome

least-privilege → PASS. excessive → FAIL on B1–B4 (B5 passes: the grant is more than sufficient).

## Limitations

- Declared grants only; effective permissions can be wider through team membership, inherited roles, or command execution on a privileged host.
- The action-to-permission table is a simplification and not an authoritative platform mapping.
